Although many PRO dry eye questionnaires (PRO-DEQs) are available, they differ greatly from each other and not all have been validated. The purpose of this study was to retrieve the PRO-DEQs present in the scientific literature by performing a descriptive analysis of them and identifying those with known validity and reliability characteristics and to perform a descriptive analysis of the geographic area, year of publication, and characteristics of the target population of the clinical studies that have used validated PRO-DEQs.

Design

Scoping review of the literature.

Methods

Searches were conducted in PubMed to retrieve PRO-DEQs published up to July 2018 and written in English, French, Italian or Spanish.

Results

One thousand six hundred two records were identified and 973 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 56 provided information on the design and validation of PRO-DEQs and 49 PRO-DEQs were identified. Twenty-two PRO-DEQs were validated (17 original and 5 modified) and 27 had no associated design, validity, and reliability studies. Most of the validated PRO-DEQs were designed in English, the number of items varies from 1 to 57, the dimensions are generally not specified, and they are self-administered. The greatest use of validated PRO-DEQs in clinical studies has been in Asia since 2010, with the Ocular Surface Disease Index being the most used. These questionnaires have been used mostly in adults, retired professionals, and people with visual diseases to diagnose DED.

Conclusions

This study aims to encourage the use of validated PRO-DEQs to guarantee the quality of the results obtained and the comparability and replicability among studies.

records.title: Topical Pharmacologic Interventions Versus Active Control, Placebo, or No Treatment for Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis: Findings From a Cochrane Systematic Review.

content.title: Topical Pharmacologic Interventions Versus Active Control, Placebo, or No Treatment for Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis: Findings From a Cochrane Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To summarize key findings from a Cochrane systematic review of the effectiveness and safety of topical pharmacologic interventions compared with active control or placebo for epidemic keratoconjunctivitis (EKC).

Design

Systematic review.

Methods

We included randomized controlled trials that compared antiseptic agents, virustatic agents, or immune-modulating topical therapies with placebo or an active control. We adhered to Cochrane methods for trial selection, data extraction, risk of bias evaluation, and data synthesis.

Results

Ten randomized controlled trials with 892 participants with acute or chronic EKC were included. Eight trials compared interventions with artificial tears or saline (n = 4) or with steroids (n = 4); two 3-arm trials contributed data to both comparisons. Estimates suggested that compared with tears, after povidone-iodine (PVP-I) alone (2 studies, 409 participants) more participants with acute EKC had resolution of symptoms (risk ratio [RR] 1.15 [95% confidence interval {CI} 1.07-1.24]) and signs (RR 3.19 [95% CI 2.29-4.45]) within 10 days. In 2 trials comparing treatments with steroid alone or steroid with levofloxacin, fewer eyes treated with PVP-I or polyvinyl alcohol iodine (PVA-I) plus steroid developed subepithelial infiltrates within 21 days (RR 0.08 [95% CI 0.01-0.55]; 69 eyes). No treatment was shown to improve resolution of infiltrates.

Conclusions

Low- to very low-level certainty of evidence suggested that PVP-I or PVA-I with steroid may confer some benefit in acute EKC, but imprecision from small sample sizes, the potential risk of bias from inadequate reporting or trial design, and variability in participant selection, outcome measurement, and reporting limit the amount and quality of evidence.

records.title: Monkeypox Virus and Ophthalmology-A Primer on the 2022 Monkeypox Outbreak and Monkeypox-Related Ophthalmic Disease.

content.title: Monkeypox Virus and Ophthalmology-A Primer on the 2022 Monkeypox Outbreak and Monkeypox-Related Ophthalmic Disease.
content.abstract:
Importance

An ongoing global monkeypox virus outbreak in 2022 includes the US and other nonendemic countries. Monkeypox ophthalmic manifestations may present to the ophthalmologist, or the ophthalmologist may be involved in comanagement. This narrative review creates a primer for the ophthalmologist of clinically relevant information regarding monkeypox, its ophthalmic manifestations, and the 2022 outbreak.

Observations

Monkeypox virus is an Orthopoxvirus (genus includes variola [smallpox] and vaccinia [smallpox vaccine]). The 2022 outbreak is of clade II (historically named West African clade), specifically subclade IIb. In addition to historic transmission patterns (skin lesions, bodily fluids, respiratory droplets), sexual transmission has also been theorized in the current outbreak due to disproportionate occurrence in men who have sex with men. Monkeypox causes a characteristic skin eruption and mucosal lesions and may cause ophthalmic disease. Monkeypox-related ophthalmic disease (MPXROD) includes a spectrum of ocular pathologies including eyelid/periorbital skin lesions, blepharoconjunctivitis, and keratitis). Smallpox vaccination may reduce MPXROD occurrence. MPXROD seems to be rarer in the 2022 outbreaks than in historical outbreaks. MPXROD may result in corneal scarring and blindness. Historical management strategies for MPXROD include lubrication and prevention/management of bacterial superinfection in monkeypox keratitis. Case reports and in vitro data for trifluridine suggest a possible role in MPXROD. Tecovirimat, cidofovoir, brincidofovir and vaccinia immune globulin intravenous may be used for systemic infection. There is a theoretical risk for monkeypox transmission by corneal transplantation, and the Eye Bank Association of America has provided guidance. Smallpox vaccines (JYNNEOS [Bavarian Nordic] and ACAM2000 [Emergent Product Development Gaithersburg Inc]) provide immunity against monkeypox.

Conclusions and relevance

The ophthalmologist may play an important role in the diagnosis and management of monkeypox. MPXROD may be associated with severe ocular and visual morbidity. As the current outbreak evolves, up-to-date guidance from public health organizations and professional societies are critical.

records.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
content.abstract: Mutations in the gene MYOC account for approximately 5% of cases of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). MYOC encodes for the protein myocilin, a multimeric secreted glycoprotein composed of N-terminal coiled-coil (CC) and leucine zipper (LZ) domains that are connected via a disordered linker to a 30 kDa olfactomedin (OLF) domain. More than 90% of glaucoma-causing mutations are localized to the OLF domain. While myocilin is expressed in numerous tissues, mutant myocilin is only associated with disease in the anterior segment of the eye, in the trabecular meshwork. The prevailing pathogenic mechanism involves a gain of toxic function whereby mutant myocilin aggregates intracellularly instead of being secreted, which causes cell stress and an early timeline for TM cell death, elevated intraocular pressure, and subsequent glaucoma-associated retinal degeneration. In this review, we focus on the work our lab has conducted over the past ∼15 years to enhance our molecular understanding of myocilin-associated glaucoma, which includes details of the molecular structure and the nature of the aggregates formed by mutant myocilin. We conclude by discussing open questions, such as predicting phenotype from genotype alone, the elusive native function of myocilin, and translational directions enabled by our work.

records.title: The physiological and pathophysiological roles of the autophagy lysosomal system in the conventional aqueous humor outflow pathway: More than cellular clean up.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The physiological and pathophysiological roles of the autophagy lysosomal system in the conventional aqueous humor outflow pathway: More than cellular clean up.
content.abstract: During the last few years, the autophagy lysosomal system is emerging as a central cellular pathway with roles in survival, acting as a housekeeper and stress response mechanism. Studies by our and other labs suggest that autophagy might play an essential role in maintaining aqueous humor outflow homeostasis, and that malfunction of autophagy in outflow pathway cells might predispose to ocular hypertension and glaucoma pathogenesis. In this review, we will collect the current knowledge and discuss the molecular mechanisms by which autophagy does or might regulate normal outflow pathway tissue function, and its response to different types of stressors (oxidative stress and mechanical stress). We will also discuss novel roles of autophagy and lysosomal enzymes in modulation of TGFβ signaling and ECM remodeling, and the link between dysregulated autophagy and cellular senescence. We will examine what we have learnt, using pre-clinical animal models about how dysregulated autophagy can contribute to disease and apply that to the current status of autophagy in human glaucoma. Finally, we will consider and discuss the challenges and the potential of autophagy as a therapeutic target for the treatment of ocular hypertension and glaucoma.

records.title: Smartphone-Based 3D Ocular Reconstruction for Automated Quantitative Blepharoptosis Evaluation.

content.title: Smartphone-Based 3D Ocular Reconstruction for Automated Quantitative Blepharoptosis Evaluation.
content.abstract:
Importance

External ocular examination is central to ptosis evaluation, yet it often relies on manual, experience-dependent measurements with variable accuracy and reproducibility.

Objective

To develop and prospectively evaluate the Digital Rulers of Ptosis (DRP), a smartphone-based 3-dimensional (3D) reconstruction system for automated quantitative external ocular assessment in blepharoptosis, including marginal reflex distance 1 (MRD1) and levator muscle function (LF), and clinical classification.

Design, setting, and participants

This diagnostic/prognostic study was conducted prospectively across 5 hospitals in 2025. Participants 3 years and older underwent smartphone video capture and same-day oculoplastic specialist assessment as the reference standard. Participants undergoing surgery received repeat specialist measurements of MRD1 and LF at 3 months postoperatively to assess recurrence.

Exposure

DRP uses a 10-second smartphone video for 3D reconstruction with metric unit conversion and real-time quality control.

Main outcomes and measures

Agreement between DRP and specialist measurements was assessed by mean absolute error (MAE) and intraclass correlation coefficient. Diagnostic performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value. For patients who underwent surgery, 3-month postoperative recurrence was assessed.

Results

Among 952 participants (1904 eyes), the mean age was 27.9 years (range, 3-86 years); 493 participants were female (51.8%) and 459 were male (48.2%). A total of 1862 eyes were included in MRD1 analysis and 1830 eyes in LF analysis after quality control. DRP demonstrated high agreement with specialist measurements for MRD1 (MAE, 0.52 mm; 95% CI, 0.50-0.54 mm) and LF (MAE, 0.95 mm; 95% CI, 0.91-0.98 mm). For diagnosing ptosis, DRP achieved an AUC of 0.97 (95% CI, 0.96-0.97). For identifying surgical approach, DRP achieved an AUC of 0.98 (95% CI, 0.97-0.98). Performance remained consistent across sex, age, and geographic region. Among 206 surgical participants (248 eyes), the 3-month postoperative recurrence rate was 7.3% (95% CI, 4.4%-11.2%; 18/248 eyes), within the lower range of previously reported rates.

Conclusions and relevance

This study found that accurate, standardized quantitative blepharoptosis assessment might be supported by commercially available smartphones, demonstrating the potential of smartphone-based 3D reconstruction for external ocular assessment and clinical decision-making. Further studies are needed to evaluate its clinical impact.

records.title: Grafting vs Intraoperative Mitomycin C for Preventing Pterygium Recurrence: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

content.title: Grafting vs Intraoperative Mitomycin C for Preventing Pterygium Recurrence: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
content.abstract:
Importance

Postoperative recurrence remains a major challenge after primary pterygium surgery, and whether grafting approaches are more effective than intraoperative mitomycin C (MMC) in reducing recurrence remains uncertain.

Objective

To determine whether grafting with conjunctival autograft (CAG) or amniotic membrane transplant (AMT) is superior to MMC in preventing 1-year recurrence after primary pterygium excision.

Design, setting, and participants

This multicenter, open-label randomized clinical trial with masked outcome assessment with 12-month follow-up was conducted at 5 tertiary hospitals in China. Enrollment and follow-up occurred between January 2016 and December 2020, and data were analyzed from September 2025 through January 2026. Patients aged 18 to 80 years with primary pterygium were enrolled and randomly assigned 1:1:1 to AMT (n = 249), MMC (n = 248), or CAG (n = 253).

Interventions

Standardized pterygium excision with conjunctival excision extending radially 4 mm from the limbus, combined with AMT, MMC, or CAG.

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was 12-month postoperative recurrence. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity, epithelial healing time, and conjunctival congestion scores.

Results

Of 750 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 57.2 [10.5] years; 487 women [64.9%]), 681 (90.8%) completed follow-up. Recurrence in the intention-to-treat analysis was 57 participants of 249 with AMT (22.9%), 34 of 248 with MMC (13.7%), and 13 of 253 with CAG (5.0%). Risk differences were 9.2 percentage points for AMT vs MMC (98.33% CI, 0.6-17.9; P = .01), 17.9 for AMT vs CAG (98.33% CI, 10.5-25.4; P < .001), and 8.7 for MMC vs CAG (98.33% CI, 2.2-15.2; P = .001). Risk ratios were 1.69 (98.33% CI, 0.99-2.91; P = .02), 4.62 (98.33% CI, 2.14-9.97; P < .001), and 2.73 (98.33% CI, 1.20-6.20; P = .004), respectively. Complete-case analyses yielded similar results. Adverse events occurred in 18 of 249 AMT participants (7.2%), 28 of 248 MMC participants (11.3%), and 16 of 253 CAG participants (6.3%), with no intervention-related serious adverse events.

Conclusions and relevance

In this randomized clinical trial, among patients undergoing primary pterygium excision, recurrence was lowest with CAG, intermediate with MMC, and highest with AMT. The moderate magnitude of the between-procedure differences makes recurrence prevention an important-but not exclusive-determinant of surgical choice and may inform individualized surgical management.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02102776.

records.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.

content.title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
content.abstract:
Importance

Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue.

Objective

To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay.

Design, setting, and participants

The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026.

Exposures

15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS).

Main outcomes and measures

Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated.

Results

Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

records.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.

content.title: Article- and Journal-Level Associations Between Altmetric Attention Scores and Citations in High-Attention Ophthalmology Publications.
content.abstract:
Importance

Altmetric Attention Scores (AAS) measure attention to scholarly articles through social media, news coverage, or policy citations. How AAS aligns with impact factors for ophthalmic peer-reviewed medical literature remains unclear.

Objective

To assess correlations between AAS and citation metrics at the article and journal levels.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional study included all citable items published between 2022 and 2023 in a subset of ophthalmology journals indexed in the 2024 Journal Citation Reports. The top 500 articles ranked by AAS were selected as a high-attention publication subset for detailed analysis.

Main outcomes and measures

The primary outcome was Spearman rank correlations between AAS rankings and normalized citation rankings (calculated as total citations divided by months elapsed since publication) at the individual article level and between an entire journal's AAS rankings and Journal Impact Factor (JIF) rankings.

Results

This study included 24 059 citable items in 99 journals. Among the top 500 high-attention articles, correlation between individual article-level AAS rankings and citation rankings was 0.08 (95% CI, -0.01 to 0.16; P = .08). At the journal level, correlation was 0.57 (95% CI, 0.41-0.69; P < .001). Correlations for predominantly clinical research-oriented journals compared with predominantly nonclinically or mixed research-oriented journals were 0.64 (95% CI, 0.46-0.79) vs 0.43 (95% CI, 0.09-0.69) (difference = 0.21; 95% CI, -0.09 to 0.60; P = .24). Multivariable analysis showed that AAS rankings were independent of document type (review vs original article: β = -10.6; 95% CI, -47.8 to 26.6; P = .58) or publication date (per month elapsed: β = 0.7; 95% CI, -1.1 to 2.5; P = .45).

Conclusions and relevance

In this cross-sectional study of high-attention ophthalmology publications, individual article-level AAS rank was not associated with citation rank, whereas journal-level Altmetric rank was moderately associated with JIF rank and greater for clinical research-oriented journals. These findings suggest that online attention and impact factor reflect partially overlapping but distinct dimensions of research dissemination and that both metrics are independent, important variables that may contribute to judging the value of peer-reviewed medical journals.

records.title: Outcomes of As-Needed Aflibercept Treatment After Complete Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

content.title: Outcomes of As-Needed Aflibercept Treatment After Complete Regression in Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.
content.abstract:
Importance

Complete polypoidal regression (termed regression) is a treatment goal in polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV), a common cause of vision loss globally. However, outcomes are controversial when treatments continue as fixed-dosing, treat-and-extend, or as-needed (PRN) regimens once regression is achieved.

Objective

To determine outcomes using PRN regimens after achieving complete polypoidal regression following an initial treatment of 3 or 6 monthly intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections in eyes with PCV.

Design, setting, and participants

This prospective cohort study took place at 4 university hospitals in Thailand. Eighty-one treatment-naive participants with PCV received 3 monthly aflibercept 2.0-mg injections. At week 12, eyes with regression underwent PRN treatment and follow-up monthly during year 1 and bimonthly during year 2. Eyes without regression at week 12 received 3 additional monthly injections and if regressed at week 24, also underwent PRN treatment and follow-up monthly through year 1 and bimonthly follow-up through year 2. Eyes without regression through week 24 received treat-and-extend regimens. These data were analyzed from August 2020 to September 2025.

Main outcomes and measures

Fluid-free interval between first visit with regression and first exudative recurrence on optical coherence tomography (OCT) by life-table analyses.

Results

Of 81 study eyes, mean [SD] age was 64 [8] years; 54% were female and 46% were male; 32 (40%) achieved regression at week 12 or 24. Of 26 eyes with regression, 13 (50%; 95% CI, 30%-70%) recurred within 2 years. Fluid-free probability after regression was 57% (95% CI, 37%-77%) at week 24 and 53% (95% CI, 33%-73%) at week 84. Among 14 eyes with recurrence, median best-corrected visual acuity change from the prior visit was -3.5 letters (IQR, -5.0 to -0.25); 3 (21%; 95% CI, 5%-51%) lost 10 or more letters, and 5 (36%; 95% CI, 13%-65%) had new hemorrhage. Post hoc exploratory analyses of eyes with complete polypoidal regression showed baseline massive subretinal hemorrhage had lower recurrence (hazard ratio [HR], 0.18; 95% CI, 0.04-0.80; P = .01). In contrast, leakage without subretinal hemorrhage may have had a higher hazard of recurrence (HR, 2.65; 95% CI, 0.89-7.94; P = .07).

Conclusions and relevance

In this study, half of the eyes with PCV achieved complete polypoidal regression remained quiescent after treatment deferral, whereas the remainder recurred. Posttreatment OCT biomarkers may help identify eyes that could benefit from continued treatment instead of PRN management.

records.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.

content.title: STRUCTURE-FUNCTION ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CONTRAST SENSITIVITY FUNCTION AND OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY FEATURES IN PATIENTS WITH IDIOPATHIC EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Investigate the structure-function relationships between epiretinal membrane (ERM) stage, tractional abnormalities, and the gap area between the ERM and the retinal surface, in relation to visual acuity and quantitative contrast sensitivity function in patients with idiopathic epiretinal membrane.

Methods

This was a retrospective, cross-sectional study involving 111 participants diagnosed with idiopathic ERM. All patients underwent a comprehensive ophthalmologic examination, spectral-domain optical coherence tomography imaging using the SPECTRALIS Heidelberg system, and contrast sensitivity (CS) testing using the quantitative contrast sensitivity function method.

Results

Progressive stages of ERM were associated with declines in both CS and visual acuity (β* = -0.45 to -0.19, P < 0.02), with CS showing a more pronounced reduction than visual acuity, especially between controls and Stage 1. Ectopic inner foveal layer thickness exhibited a similar pattern of decline in both visual acuity (β* = 0.42, P < 0.001) and CS (β* = -0.46 to -0.18, all P < 0.02). By contrast, SUKIMA showed no significant association with any of the visual measurements assessed. Among the tractional abnormalities, the cotton ball sign correlated with diminished vision, particularly reflected by a notable drop in CS at the highest spatial frequencies tested with reduced CS at 12 cycles per degree (β* = -0.44, P = 0.02) and 18 cycles per degree (β* = -0.46, P = 0.02).

Conclusion

Quantitative contrast sensitivity function testing is particularly important for assessing visual function in ERM development, especially in the early stages.

records.title: Treatment of Retinal/Choroidal Vascular Diseases by Sustained Delivery of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.

content.title: Treatment of Retinal/Choroidal Vascular Diseases by Sustained Delivery of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review current investigational strategies using sustained delivery of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) for the treatment of retinal and choroidal vascular diseases.

Design

Narrative review.

Methods

A comprehensive review of preclinical and clinical studies evaluating the safety, efficacy, and durability of VEGF receptor TKIs delivered via sustained-release platforms, including intravitreal hydrogel implants, suprachoroidal injections, subcutaneous delivery systems, and oral formulations.

Results

Multiple VEGF receptor TKIs, including axitinib, sunitinib, vorolanib, and dendranib, are under evaluation for sustained treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration, diabetic macular edema, and diabetic retinopathy. Delivery platforms such as bioerodible implants (OTX-TKI/axitinib, EYP-1901/vorolanib), suprachoroidal injections (CLS-AX/axitinib), microparticle suspensions (GB-102/sunitinib), and oral or subcutaneous therapies (X-82, D-4517.2) have demonstrated variable degrees of treatment durability, reduction in anti-VEGF injection burden, and maintenance of anatomic and functional outcomes in early phase studies. Safety profiles have generally been favorable, although certain formulations showed dose-dependent adverse effects.

Conclusions

Sustained delivery of VEGF receptor TKIs represents a promising therapeutic paradigm for retinal and choroidal vascular diseases, potentially reducing treatment burden while maintaining efficacy. Continued evaluation through larger, controlled clinical trials is essential to validate these early findings and define the role of these agents in clinical practice.

records.title: TFOS DEWS III: Diagnostic Methodology.

content.title: TFOS DEWS III: Diagnostic Methodology.
content.abstract: A standard approach to the diagnosis of dry eye disease across eye care practitioners is critical to reassuring the patient, providing consistency between practitioners and informing governments as to the true prevalence and resulting healthcare needs. The Tear Film & Ocular Surface Society (TFOS) Dry Eye Workshop (DEWS) III has reviewed the evidence-base since their previous reports published in 2017 and revised the definition to "Dry eye is a multifactorial, symptomatic disease characterized by a loss of homeostasis of the tear film and/or ocular surface, in which tear film instability and hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities are etiological factors." Key features from the definition include that dry eye disease is multifactorial, is a disease and not a syndrome and is always symptomatic. Differential diagnosis and ocular examination guidance is given along with the risk factors that should be discussed with the patient. The recommended screening questionnaire is the OSDI-6 with a cut-off score ≥4. A positive result together with a non-invasive breakup time <10s or alternatively tear film hyperosmolarity (≥308mOsm/L in either eye or an interocular difference >8mOsm/L) or alternatively >5 corneal fluorescein and/or >9 conjunctival lissamine green punctate spots and/or lid margin lissamine green staining of ≥2mm length & ≥25 % width, gives a diagnosis of dry eye. Subclassification was separated into tear film deficiencies (lipid, aqueous and mucin/glycocalyx), eyelid anomalies (blink/lid closure and lid margin) and ocular surface abnormalities (anatomical misalignment, neural dysfunction, ocular surface cell damage/disruption and primary inflammation/oxidative stress) components, with appropriate clinical tests and cut-offs provided to identify these etiological drivers in an individual, to inform appropriate management and therapy.

records.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Toward an internationally accepted standard for reading charts.
content.abstract: Patients who suffer from sight-threatening eye diseases share a desire to regain a comfortable reading ability. In light of the modern advances achieved in ophthalmic diagnosis and therapy, and because a significant lack of comparability between reading charts still exists, there is an increasing need for a worldwide standard in the form of a norm for diagnostic reading charts. Already, applied advancements such as digital print, which allow a calibration of the print sizes of reading charts in correctly progressing geometric proportions by using the actual height of a lower case "x" in millimeters (x-height), and psychophysically standardizing reading charts and their test items by applying modern statistical methods have significantly contributed to establishing a norm for reading charts. In 2020, a proposal of the British delegation was accepted by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) group "Visual Optics and Optical Instruments," and a working group was established. Bearing in mind the efforts of the ISO with regard to an international norm, this review article is intended to (a) give an overview of the historical background and related normative approaches for diagnostic reading tests used in ophthalmology and optometry, (b) explain psychophysical and technical concerns, and (c) discuss the possibilities and limits of concepts that seem relevant to developing a modern standard for reading charts.

records.title: Size Matters.

content.title: Size Matters.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To describe the ideal size of a laser iridotomy and to discuss its importance.

Design

Perspective.

Methods

Articles in ophthalmology literature on this topic were reviewed, and commentary is provided based on the authors' experiences.

Results

An ideal laser iridotomy size is 200 µm or larger, especially in eyes with uveitis. The final size of an iridotomy must be confirmed after the effects of the pilocarpine has worn off and the pupil is not being constricted by light. A location of the iridotomy furthest from the lid margin may reduce the chances of dysphotopsias and thus allow for an adequate-sized iridotomy.

Conclusions

An iridotomy of an ideal size is needed to reduce the pressure differential on both sides of the iris so as to be effective in eliminating pupillary block.

records.title: Hypotony Failure Criteria in Glaucoma Surgical Studies and Their Influence on Surgery Success.

content.title: Hypotony Failure Criteria in Glaucoma Surgical Studies and Their Influence on Surgery Success.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Review hypotony failure criteria used in glaucoma surgical outcome studies and evaluate their impact on success rates.

Design

Systematic literature review and application of hypotony failure criteria to 2 retrospective cohorts.

Participants

A total of 934 eyes and 1765 eyes undergoing trabeculectomy and deep sclerectomy (DS) with a median follow-up of 41.4 and 45.4 months, respectively.

Methods

Literature-based hypotony failure criteria were applied to patient cohorts. Intraocular pressure (IOP)-related success was defined as follows: (A) IOP ≤ 21 mmHg with ≥ 20% IOP reduction; (B) IOP ≤ 18 mmHg with ≥ 20% reduction; (C) IOP ≤ 15 mmHg with ≥ 25% reduction; and (D) IOP ≤ 12 mmHg with ≥ 30% reduction. Failure was defined as IOP exceeding these criteria in 2 consecutive visits > 3 months after surgery, loss of light perception, additional IOP-lowering surgery, or hypotony. Cox regression estimated failure risk for different hypotony criteria, using no hypotony as a reference. Analyses were conducted for each criterion and hypotony type (i.e., numerical [IOP threshold], clinical [clinical manifestations], and mixed [combination of numerical or clinical criteria]).

Main outcome measures

Hazard ratio (HR) for failure risk.

Results

Of 2503 studies found, 278 were eligible, with 99 studies (35.6%) lacking hypotony failure criteria. Numerical hypotony was predominant (157 studies [56.5%]). Few studies used clinical hypotony (3 isolated [1.1%]; 19 combined with low IOP [6.8%]). Forty-nine different criteria were found, with IOP < 6 mmHg, IOP < 6 mmHg on ≥ 2 consecutive visits after 3 months, and IOP < 5 mmHg being the most common (41 [14.7%], 38 [13.7%], and 13 [4.7%] studies, respectively). In both cohorts, numerical hypotony posed the highest risk of failure (HR, 1.51-1.21 for criteria A to D; P < 0.001), followed by mixed hypotony (HR, 1.41-1.20 for criteria A to D; P < 0.001), and clinical hypotony (HR, 1.12-1.04; P < 0.001). Failure risk varied greatly with various hypotony definitions, with the HR ranging from 1.02 to 10.79 for trabeculectomy and 1.00 to 8.36 for DS.

Conclusions

Hypotony failure criteria are highly heterogenous in the glaucoma literature, with few studies focusing on clinical manifestations. Numerical hypotony yields higher failure rates than clinical hypotony and can underestimate glaucoma surgery success rates. Standardizing failure criteria with an emphasis on clinically relevant hypotony manifestations is needed.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Mechanisms of blood-retinal barrier disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy.
content.abstract: Blood-retinal barrier (BRB) disruption is a common accompaniment of intermediate, posterior and panuveitis causing leakage into the retina and macular oedema resulting in vision loss. It is much less common in anterior uveitis or in patients with intraocular lymphoma who may have marked signs of intraocular inflammation. New drugs used for chemotherapy (cytarabine, immune checkpoint inhibitors, BRAF inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, bispecific anti-EGFR inhibitors, MET receptor inhibitors and Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) can also cause different types of uveitis and BRB disruption. As malignant disease itself can cause uveitis, particularly from breast, lung and gastrointestinal tract cancers, it can be clinically difficult to sort out the cause of BRB disruption. Immunosuppression due to malignant disease and/or chemotherapy can lead to infection which can also cause BRB disruption and intraocular infection. In this paper we address the pathophysiology of BRB disruption related to intraocular inflammation and malignancy, methods for estimating the extent and effect of the disruption and examine why some types of intraocular inflammation and malignancy cause BRB disruption and others do not. Understanding this may help sort and manage these patients, as well as devise future therapeutic approaches.

records.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Investing in vision: Innovation in retinal therapeutics and the influence on venture capital investment.
content.abstract: Since the groundbreaking approval of the first anti-VEGF therapy in 2004, the retinal therapeutics field has undergone a remarkable transformation, witnessing a surge in novel, disease-modifying therapeutics for a broad spectrum of retinal diseases, extending beyond exudative VEGF-driven conditions. The surge in scientific advancement and the pressing, unmet, medical need have captured the attention of venture capital investors, who have collectively invested close to $10 billion in research and development of new retinal therapeutics between 2004 and 2023. Notably, the field of exudative diseases has gradually shifted away from trying to outcompete anti-VEGF therapeutics towards lowering the overall treatment burden by reducing injection frequency. Simultaneously, a new era has emerged in the non-exudative field, targeting prevalent conditions like dry AMD and rare indications such as Retinitis pigmentosa. This has led to promising drug candidates in development, culminating in the landmark approval of Luxturna for a rare form of Retinitis pigmentosa. The validation of new mechanisms, such as the complement pathway in dry AMD has paved the way for the approvals of Syvovre (Apellis) and Izervay (Iveric/Astellas), marking the first two therapies for this condition. In this comprehensive review, we share our view on the cumulative lessons from the past two decades in developing retinal therapeutics, covering both positive achievements and challenges. We also contextualize the investments, strategic partnering deals, and acquisitions of biotech companies, pharmaceutical companies venture capital investors in retinal therapeutics, respectively. Finally, we provide an outlook and potentially a forward-looking roadmap on novel retinal therapeutics, highlighting the emergence of potential new intervention strategies, such as cell-based therapies, gene editing, and combination therapies. We conclude that upcoming developments have the potential to further stimulate venture capital investments, which ultimately could facilitate the development and delivery of new therapies to patients in need.

records.title: Impact of Vision Impairment and Ocular Morbidity and Their Treatment on Depression and Anxiety in Children: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Impact of Vision Impairment and Ocular Morbidity and Their Treatment on Depression and Anxiety in Children: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Topic

This systematic review and meta-analysis summarizes existing evidence to establish whether vision impairment, ocular morbidity, and their treatment are associated with depression and anxiety in children.

Clinical relevance

Understanding and quantifying these associations support early detection and management of mental health symptoms in children with vision impairment and ocular morbidity. Additionally, this review provides evidence in favor of insurance coverage for timely strabismus surgery.

Methods

We searched 9 electronic databases from inception through February 18, 2021, including observational and interventional studies assessing whether vision impairment, ocular morbidity, or both and their treatment are associated with depression, anxiety, or both in children. We used narrative synthesis and meta-analysis with the residual maximum likelihood method. A protocol was registered and published on The International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (identifier: CRD42021233323).

Results

Among 28 992 studies, 28 956 studies (99.9%) were excluded as duplicates or unrelated content. Among 36 remaining studies, 21 studies (58.3%) were observational studies concerning vision impairment, 8 studies (22.2%) were observational studies concerning strabismus, and 7 studies (19.4%) were interventional studies. Vision impaired children demonstrated significantly higher scores of depression (standard mean difference [SMD], 0.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.26-0.89; 11 studies) and anxiety (SMD, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.40-0.83; 14 studies) than normally sighted children. In particular, children with myopia demonstrated higher scores of depression (SMD, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.36-0.81; 6 studies) than normally sighted children. Strabismus surgery significantly improved symptoms of depression (SMD, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.12-1.06; 3 studies) and anxiety (SMD, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.25-1.14; 4 studies) in children.

Conclusion

Among children, vision impairment is associated with greater symptoms of depression and anxiety. Surgical treatment of strabismus improved these symptoms. Further randomized controlled trials exploring the impact of public health measures for myopia correction on mental health in children are needed. Scaling up access to strabismus surgery could improve the mental health of affected children.

records.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI)-Associated Retinal and Choroidal Adverse Reactions.

content.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor (ICI)-Associated Retinal and Choroidal Adverse Reactions.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To summarize and categorize postulated mechanisms of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-mediated retinal and choroidal inflammation and discuss resulting implications for evaluation and management of these adverse reactions.

Design

Targeted literature review with interpretation and perspective METHODS: We performed a review of selected literature describing immune-mediated retinal and choroidal adverse reactions associated with ICI therapy, synthesizing and categorizing the likely underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Based on these mechanistic categories, we provide perspective on a rational approach to the evaluation of patients with ICI-associated inflammatory disorders of the retina and choroid.

Results

ICI-induced posterior segment adverse reactions can be categorized into 3 major mechanisms of unintended, targeted inflammation that share similarities to immunotherapy-related adverse events (irAEs) seen in other organ systems. In Type 1 reactions, T cell activation by ICIs can result in cross-reactivity of anti-tumor T cells with ocular tissues (Type 1a) or expansion of eye-specific T cells in predisposed individuals (Type 1b), leading to ocular inflammation that mimics known uveitic conditions. In Type 2 reactions, nonspecific ocular or systemic inflammation exacerbated by ICI use can cause retinal vasculitis through a "bystander" mechanism, potentially resulting in vision-threatening vascular occlusions. Finally, in Type 3 reactions, ICI use can prompt autoantibody-mediated inflammation and/or exacerbation of paraneoplastic processes likely related to T cell driven expansion of B cell populations.

Conclusions

Although relatively uncommon, posterior segment inflammatory disorders associated with systemic ICI therapy may be vision-threatening if not identified and treated appropriately. We propose that the pathogenic mechanisms underlying these chorioretinopathies falls into 3 major categories involving inadvertent T cell mediated inflammation. Visual prognosis with appropriate treatment is generally favorable, but some reactions, such as longstanding exudative retinal detachments and ICI-induced occlusive retinal vasculitis, can result in permanent visual defects.

records.title: Efficacy of a new water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% solution for optimizing the ocular surface in patients with dry eye and cataract.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Efficacy of a new water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% solution for optimizing the ocular surface in patients with dry eye and cataract.
content.abstract: This is a pooled analysis from 2 phase III clinical trials investigating a water-free topical cyclosporine 0.1% for the treatment of moderate to severe dry eye. The analyses included 1162 patients: 35% with cataract, 20% with pseudophakia, and 45% without cataract. Demographics or baseline characteristics were comparable across groups except for age and vision. The cyclosporine-treated patients achieved large mean improvements from baseline by day 15: -3.7 in patients without cataract, -3.2 in patients with cataract, and -3.1 in pseudophakic patients. These improvements were statistically significantly higher compared with the respective vehicle groups. In the cataract subgroup, 59% of patients treated with cyclosporine achieved ≥3 grade improvements in corneal staining score, as early as day 15. The magnitude of the effect and early onset of action make this new cyclosporine solution a promising candidate for preoperative management of ocular surface in patients undergoing cataract surgery.

records.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo) in the retina and implications for ocular diseases.
content.abstract: Translocator protein (18 kDa) (Tspo), formerly known as peripheral benzodiazepine receptor is a highly conserved transmembrane protein primarily located in the outer mitochondrial membrane. In the central nervous system (CNS), especially in glia cells, Tspo is upregulated upon inflammation. Consequently, Tspo was used as a tool for diagnostic in vivo imaging of neuroinflammation in the brain and as a potential therapeutic target. Several synthetic Tspo ligands have been explored as immunomodulatory and neuroprotective therapy approaches. Although the function of Tspo and how its ligands exert these beneficial effects is not fully clear, it became a research topic of interest, especially in ocular diseases in the past few years. This review summarizes state-of-the-art knowledge of Tspo expression and its proposed functions in different cells of the retina including microglia, retinal pigment epithelium and Müller cells. Tspo is involved in cytokine signaling, oxidative stress and reactive oxygen species production, calcium signaling, neurosteroid synthesis, energy metabolism, and cholesterol efflux. We also highlight recent developments in preclinical models targeting Tspo and summarize the relevance of Tspo biology for ocular and retinal diseases. We conclude that glial upregulation of Tspo in different ocular pathologies and the use of Tspo ligands as promising therapeutic approaches in preclinical studies underline the importance of Tspo as a potential disease-modifying protein.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.

content.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression.
content.abstract:
Purpose of review

This review examines the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) models for the detection and prediction of glaucomatous progression.

Recent findings

Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed to analyze longitudinal data from optic disc photographs, optical coherence tomography images, and visual field tests to identify worsening glaucoma. Recent AI research has also expanded beyond simply detecting progression to predicting future disease trajectories. These approaches may provide more efficient assessment than clinician review alone.

Summary

AI models can rapidly analyze large volumes of clinical data to support individualized glaucoma management; these models can guide treatment intensity and follow-up intervals by detecting and predicting glaucomatous progression. However, significant hurdles to clinical adoption remain, including the "black box" nature of AI, absence of a universally accepted reference standard for progression, variable data quality, and limited generalizability across populations and clinical settings. AI is poised to function as a clinical decision support tool rather than a replacement for clinicians. Prospective studies are needed to determine the impact of AI in improving patient outcomes, clinical efficiency, and healthcare costs.

records.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Assessment of peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus using a deep learning-based approach.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate peripapillary choroidal microvascular structure in patients with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) using a novel deep learning-based approach, and to evaluate longitudinal changes following shunt surgery.

Methods

In this prospective study, 22 patients with iNPH and 22 age-matched healthy controls underwent peripapillary optical coherence tomography (OCT). A deep learning-based ResUNet model enabled choroidal segmentation and quantification of total choroidal area (TCA), stromal choroidal area (SCA), luminal choroidal area (LCA), and the choroidal vascularity index (CVI). Measurements were compared between groups and reassessed in iNPH patients after ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery.

Results

Forty-four eyes of 22 iNPH patients and 44 eyes of 22 controls were analyzed. iNPH eyes exhibited significantly greater mean SCA compared to controls (adjusted p < 0.05). On the other hand, CVI remained comparable between groups. Following a mean follow-up of approximately 12 months after shunt surgery, mean SCA showed significant reduction (adjusted p < 0.05), whereas CVI remained unchanged.

Conclusions

iNPH was associated with peripapillary choroidal changes, predominantly involving the stromal compartment. Deep learning-based OCT analysis may provide a noninvasive approach for quantifying peripapillary choroidal microstructure, although the clinical relevance of these findings remains to be established.

records.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.

content.title: Early Diagnosis and Prognosis of Corneal and Ocular Surface Pathologies Using Artificial Intelligence: A State-of-the-art Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aims to elucidate the expanding role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the early diagnosis of corneal and ocular surface diseases. AI has the potential to enhance diagnostic precision, streamline clinical workflows, and facilitate disease detection before clinical manifestations become evident.

Methods

A narrative literature review was conducted to assess the impact of AI and machine learning in corneal disease preclinical diagnosis. A comprehensive search in PubMed was performed using key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "deep learning," "corneal diseases," and "early diagnosis." Eligible studies were those published in English over the last decade that focused on AI-driven diagnostic approaches and prognostic modeling. Case reports, nonoriginal studies, and those with minimal AI integration were excluded. Data extraction emphasized AI methodologies, imaging techniques, diagnostic performance metrics, and clinical relevance.

Results

AI-powered machine learning models analyze vast imaging datasets, detecting subclinical abnormalities imperceptible to conventional diagnostic methods. This capability is particularly significant in early keratoconus detection, dystrophies, infectious keratitis, conjunctival neoplasia, and other corneal pathologies such as dry eye or Steven-Johnson disease, where subtle morphological changes precede clinically apparent disease.

Conclusions

The integration of AI into corneal disease diagnostics and management could mark in the future a transformative shift in Ophthalmology, offering precision, efficiency, and scalability. By facilitating early disease detection and individualized patient assessments, AI minimizes diagnostic inconsistencies and accelerates clinical decision making. Continuous algorithm refinement and real-world validation are crucial to maximizing AI's clinical utility. To fully harness AI's potential, multidisciplinary collaboration among ophthalmologists, data scientists, and regulatory bodies is imperative to address standardization, ethical concerns, and implementation barriers. As AI-driven technologies continue to evolve, they will redefine the standard of care in corneal disease diagnosis, therapeutic precision, and patient outcomes.

records.title: Recent advances in optical coherence tomography for glaucoma: from macular imaging and optical coherence tomography angiography to artificial intelligence and portable platforms.

content.title: Recent advances in optical coherence tomography for glaucoma: from macular imaging and optical coherence tomography angiography to artificial intelligence and portable platforms.
content.abstract:
Purpose of review

Recent advances are extending optical coherence tomography (OCT)'s role beyond conventional structural metrics. This review summarizes recent developments in macular OCT, OCT angiography (OCTA), artificial intelligence (AI), and portable/home-based OCT.

Recent findings

Macular ganglion-cell measures (ganglion-cell-inner plexiform layer, ganglion cell complex) increasingly complement retinal nerve fiber layer assessment, offering greater diagnostic/prognostic value in advanced glaucoma, myopia, and certain glaucoma subtypes. OCTA is emerging as a complementary vascular biomarker; peripapillary vessel density shows the most consistent link to progression, with early evidence that vascular changes may precede detectable structural or functional decline. Deep learning models increasingly use raw or multimodal imaging rather than summary parameters; foundation and multimodal architectures (e.g., RETFound-based) show strong diagnostic performance and improved generalizability across demographics and disease severity. However, AI-based progression prediction remains less robust than cross-sectional diagnosis, especially under external validation. Portable/home-based OCT may extend monitoring beyond the clinic, though clinical utility remains investigational.

Summary

The field is moving toward multimodal, longitudinal, AI-supported glaucoma assessment integrating structural, vascular, and functional biomarkers rather than interpreting them in isolation. Key priorities for translation include standardized acquisition and analysis across devices, large and diverse external validation cohorts, interpretable models, and evidence that AI and remote imaging improve clinically meaningful outcomes. These developments should make OCT increasingly central to earlier detection and individualized monitoring of glaucoma, but none currently replace established structural and functional assessment or clinical judgment.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks.
content.abstract: The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, and surgical workflow analysis. We propose a conceptual multimodal pipeline comprising data ingestion, preprocessing and harmonization, feature representation, multimodal fusion, forecasting, explainability, and validation. A structured evidence grading framework classifies each clinical task by evidence level, consistency, and clinical readiness. We further catalog public datasets, challenge benchmarks, and five reporting standards: TRIPOD-AI, CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and CLAIM. Computer-aided detection and optical diagnosis demonstrate the highest maturity with Level 1 evidence from randomized controlled trials, while computational pathology, radiogenomics, and metastasis prediction remain at Level 2 with retrospective validation (internal or external). Microbiome screening, nanotechnology diagnostics, and surgical phase recognition are exploratory. The principal barriers to clinical adoption are domain shift, data scarcity, calibration, prospective validation, and workflow integration. We conclude that clinically useful artificial intelligence requires robust external validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable outputs, standardized reporting, and a structured translational pathway from retrospective evidence through regulatory clearance to post-deployment monitoring.

records.title: Image-Based AI for the Diagnosis of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Image-Based AI for the Diagnosis of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is one of the major causes of preventable blindness in premature infants. Early screening, accurate diagnosis, and severity classification are crucial for reducing irreversible visual impairment. Recently, image-based AI models have been widely applied to ROP screening, diagnosis, and severity classification. However, the model architecture, data source, validation method, and diagnostic task vary across studies. Consequently, the overall diagnostic efficiency and clinical utility of deep learning (DL) remain to be systematically assessed.

Objective

This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of image-based AI for ROP by disease type, validation method, model type, and use of transfer learning (TL).

Methods

We performed a systematic search across Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Cochrane Library as of October 12, 2026, to identify studies investigating image-based AI for ROP detection or clinical subtype classification. The risk of bias (RoB) of included studies was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using bivariate mixed-effects models, with analyses stratified by diagnostic task and validation method.

Results

Sixty-two studies contributed 185 contingency tables. For normal vs ROP, pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.96) and specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.97). For normal vs treatment-requiring ROP (TR-ROP), sensitivity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.91-0.99) and specificity was 0.74 (95% CI 0.66-0.80). For mild vs severe ROP, specificity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.59-0.90). In external validation, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.97) and 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.90), respectively, while the corresponding estimates were 0.95 (95% CI 0.93-0.96) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) in internal validation. For DL and conventional machine learning (ML) models, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98), respectively, while specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-0.94), respectively. With and without TL, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.97), respectively, while specificity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.95), respectively.

Conclusions

Image-based AI may have high sensitivity for ROP assessment, but its specificity is lower for identifying TR-ROP and in the external-validation subgroup. Given the predominance of retrospective studies, heterogeneity, and limited external validation, current evidence supports AI as an adjunct to screening and referral, with clinicians retaining responsibility for diagnostic and treatment decisions. Prospective, multicenter external validation is needed.

Trial registration

PROSPERO CRD420261418502; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418502.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.

content.title: Mapping Research on AI-Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support Systems: a Bibliometric Study Integrating Google Trends and Content Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Research on artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis and clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) is expanding, but integrated evidence on publication patterns, keyword trajectories, online search activity, and methodological characteristics remains limited.

Objective

To characterize AI-CDSS research by integrating bibliometric analysis, Google Trends comparison, and structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications.

Methods

Scholarly interest was assessed using bibliometric analysis of Web of Science records from 2016 through August 2026, including author-keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and reference co-citation, whereas Google Trends was used to characterize online search activity. A structured content analysis of citation-ranked publications was conducted to examine applications, methodological characteristics, and reported limitations.

Results

We analyzed 19,809 included publications from 2016 through August 2026. Output rose approximately 21-fold, from 193 records in 2016 to 4,082 in 2025. Output was geographically concentrated within the included corpus, with a Gini coefficient of 0.869. Among records with identifiable corresponding-author country or territory, China, the United States, and India accounted for 61.33%. Scientific Reports was the most frequent source (n = 916). Frequent artificial intelligence- and diagnosis-related keywords included machine learning (n = 5,666), deep learning (n = 4,022), and computer-aided diagnosis (n = 1,512). Bibliographic coupling identified 15 publication communities, and reference co-citation identified seven reference communities. In the monthly level-series comparison, 9 of 10 keyword concepts exhibited significant associations with Google Trends relative search interest, but none of the 10 first-difference associations remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Content analysis of 215 citation-ranked publications, including 191 empirical publications, showed frequent use of convolutional neural networks in diagnostic and radiology applications. Common limitations included limited external validation, infrequent calibration reporting, and sparse workflow-level or impact evaluation.

Conclusion

AI-CDSS research has rapidly expanded around machine learning, deep learning, and diagnostic applications, but the analyzed citation-ranked publications provide more evidence of methodological development than of clinical deployment. Integrating bibliometric, search-activity, and content-based perspectives shows limited short-term correspondence between online search activity and scholarly keyword use and highlights the need to move beyond model development toward independent external validation, prospective workflow and patient-outcome evaluation, calibration, fairness, and postdeployment monitoring.

records.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.

content.title: Automated assessment of healthcare de-escalation communication skills in a conversational AI virtual reality simulation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Digital health training environments increasingly require scalable methods for assessing communication skills in realistic, interactive scenarios. This paper presents a comparative study of automated assessment approaches within a conversational AI virtual reality simulation designed for verbal de-escalation training.

Methods

A total of 20 nursing students completed the simulation, where their spoken responses were captured and converted to text through a speech-to-text system, and were evaluated across 11 de-escalation competencies. The evaluation compared three fine-tuned deep learning models (BERT, RoBERTa, and XLNet) with a modified RATAS, a rubric-driven framework that leverages large language models. Two experiments were conducted: one using controlled 100-item validation datasets for each section, and another using the real-world responses collected during the user study.

Results

On the validation datasets, the deep learning models achieved the highest performance, with RoBERTa obtaining an average accuracy of 0.9927, followed by BERT at 0.9900 and XLNet at 0.9790, while RATAS achieved 0.8554. On the student-response dataset, performance decreased for all approaches, with RoBERTa obtaining 0.8590 accuracy, RATAS 0.8181, BERT 0.8000, and XLNet 0.7681.

Discussion

These results suggest that transformer-based models perform best under controlled conditions, whereas RATAS demonstrated stability in grading across different dataset types. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of integrating deep learning and rubric-driven LLM-based automated assessment approaches for communication and de-escalation training in nursing education.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes.
