Given the well-documented effects of sex hormones on skeletal muscle, including on muscle mass, regeneration, and recovery, our review was aimed at assessing the impact of OCPs on skeletal muscle physiology in female humans and animals. We performed a literature search, title through full text screening, and citation search in accordance with PROSPERO guidelines. Rigor and reproducibility were assessed using the Modified Downs and Black Checklist. Meta-analyses were performed to assess the impact of OCPs on skeletal muscle outcomes. Although our search included both clinical and preclinical studies, the 40 included studies were all clinical, with no identified preclinical studies. Studies focused on young (20-30 yr) sedentary to active females with a healthy BMI (18-27 kg/m<sup>2</sup>) and included primarily strength and serum-based outcomes. All studies were retrospective and level III evidence. Notably, despite this literature spanning from the 1990s to 2025, rigor was in the 69th ± 6.5 percentile, and there was no correlation with rigor and year of publication. Meta-analyses did not detect an effect of OCPs on examined outcome measures; however, heterogeneity was high, suggesting the lack of rejection of the null hypothesis may be driven by variations in studies, making it challenging to draw conclusions. Taken together, we recommend prospective preclinical and well-controlled clinical studies to examine the impact of OCPs on skeletal muscle in the setting of injury, disease, and varying demographics. Our ultimate goal is to understand sex-based differences in skeletal muscle health and empower females with reliable information to inform decisions about their health. This systematic review and meta-analysis was a step toward the goal of understanding the role of OCPs on skeletal muscle health.

records.title: Effect of virtual reality-based training on postural balance in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Effect of virtual reality-based training on postural balance in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Virtual reality, an emerging rehabilitation technology, is increasingly used to improve postural balance in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders. This review evaluated the effectiveness of virtual reality interventions for improving postural balance in this population based on randomized controlled trials.

Materials and methods

PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang were systematically searched from database inception through November 6, 2025, for English- and Chinese-language randomized controlled trials examining virtual reality-based interventions on objective measures of postural balance in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and the certainty of evidence was appraised according to the GRADE approach. Pooled standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals were computed using the meta package in R (version 4.5.1), and heterogeneity, subgroup, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

Results

Ten RCTs involving 372 participants were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that virtual reality-based interventions were associated with statistically significant improvements in postural balance compared with control conditions (SMD = 0.30, 95%CI [0.09, 0.51], p = 0.004). Although trials with shorter session durations, lower weekly training frequencies, and shorter intervention periods appeared to yield larger effects, subgroup analyses failed to identify statistically significant between-subgroup differences.

Conclusion

This systematic review and meta-analysis indicates that virtual reality-based interventions may enhance postural balance in children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental disorders. However, the certainty of evidence remains limited owing to the paucity of included trials and methodological limitations. Future large-scale randomized controlled trials with extended follow-up periods and standardized balance assessments are warranted to corroborate these findings and optimize intervention parameters.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251135718, CRD420251135718.

records.title: Navigating the AI Landscape in Medical Imaging: A Critical Analysis of Technologies, Implementation, and Implications.

content.title: Navigating the AI Landscape in Medical Imaging: A Critical Analysis of Technologies, Implementation, and Implications.
content.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of medical imaging outpaces the available radiologist workforce, risking timely diagnosis. Comprehensive artificial intelligence (AI) that integrates multimodal imaging data, clinical notes, and large language models has the potential to support radiologists. Accordingly, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared more than 770 AI medical devices that focus on radiology, primarily based on deep learning. However, algorithm development and validation remain challenging. Limitations include sparse expert-annotated data and regulatory hurdles. Clinical implementation and the adaptation of the radiologic community is also lagging behind. Additionally, technical barriers exist regarding data availability, large language model explainability, deep learning model generalization, and clinical integration. Advances in few-shot learning, self-supervised models, and centralized platforms may support consolidated AI ecosystems. Although progress has been made, much work is still needed on data infrastructure, responsible clinical translation, and workflow integration. Continuous multidisciplinary efforts are required to optimize AI safety and truly augment radiologists' work through comprehensive solutions. By overcoming the remaining challenges, AI may strengthen health care systems through improved diagnosis. This review addresses integration challenges, pathways for responsible progress, and the viewpoints of all stakeholders.

records.title: Multidimensional Effects of Telemedicine on Patients With Spinal Cord Injury: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

content.title: Multidimensional Effects of Telemedicine on Patients With Spinal Cord Injury: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
content.abstract:
Background

Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes persistent physical and psychological impairments and is associated with reduced quality of life. Telemedicine may improve rehabilitation access and follow-up care, but its effectiveness across multiple outcome domains in SCI remains uncertain.

Objective

This study aimed to evaluate the effects of telemedicine interventions on psychological health, quality of life, sleep, functional independence, and participation, and pain intensity in individuals with SCI.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, and Cochrane CENTRAL until 17 February 2026. We included English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of telemedicine interventions in individuals with SCI. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; Cochrane) tool. Random-effects meta-analyses used the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance. Effects were summarized as standardized mean differences (SMD) or mean differences (MD) with 95% CIs. For main meta-analyses, 95% prediction intervals were reported when at least 5 studies were available, but not for analyses with fewer than 5 studies or for subgroup meta-analyses. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

Results

We included 33 studies (35 reports). Telemedicine improved the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF) social domain (MD 3.27, 95% CI 0.64 to 5.89; P=.03) and sleep quality at 3 months (MD -2.24, 95% CI -3.82 to -0.67; P=.04). Depressive symptoms also improved in the >3-≤6 months follow-up subgroup (SMD -0.31, 95% CI -0.57 to -0.04; P=.03). Overall effects for depressive symptoms were not significant (SMD -0.11, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.05; prediction interval -0.37 to 0.15; P=.16; I²=36.3%), while findings for anxiety, other WHOQOL-BREF domains, sleep quality at 1 month, functional outcomes, and pain intensity generally favored telemedicine but did not reach statistical significance. Approximately half of the studies were rated as low risk overall on RoB 2, with most remaining studies rated as having some concerns and a smaller subset rated as high risk. GRADE certainty was high for the >3-≤6-month depressive-symptoms subgroup, moderate for the WHOQOL-BREF social domain, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and low for depressive symptoms overall, anxiety, and pain intensity.

Conclusions

Telemedicine may improve selected outcomes in SCI, with the most consistent evidence for social aspects of quality of life, sleep after sustained intervention exposure, and a more favorable effect on depressive symptoms in midterm follow-up subgroup analyses. These results suggest telemedicine as a practical adjunct for extending SCI rehabilitation access and continuity. Further trials should focus on optimizing intervention components, intensity, and patient targeting.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based magnetic resonance imaging for preoperative staging of patients with endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based magnetic resonance imaging for preoperative staging of patients with endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

To systematically collect all literature on the value of artificial intelligence (AI)-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for preoperative prediction of myometrial invasion and cervical stroma invasion in patients with endometrial cancer and conduct a meta-analysis to provide the latest and most comprehensive synthesis of current research findings.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library databases up to March 2025. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool. Statistical analyses were primarily conducted using Stata15.0 and Review Manager 5.4.1 software. Outcomes included combined Sen, Spe, +LR, -LR, DOR, and their 95% CI. The SROC curve was plotted, and the AUC was calculated. The Deeks' funnel plot was used to detect publication bias and assumed small-study effects.

Results

Finally, 8 studies (including 13 cohorts) were included. The overall performance of AI-based MRI for the prediction of deep myometrial invasion showed a combined Sen, Spe, +LR, -LR, DOR, and AUC value of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.75-0.85), 0.81 (95% CI: 0.64-0.91), 4.2 (95% CI: 2.0-8.5), 0.24 (95% CI: 0.17-0.34), 17 (95% CI: 6-47), and 0.83 (95% CI: 0.80-0.86), respectively. The overall performance of AI-based MRI for the prediction of cervical stroma invasion showed a combined Sen, Spe, +LR, -LR, DOR, and AUC value of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.55-0.91), 0.86 (95% CI: 0.79-0.91), 5.6 (95% CI: 4.3-7.4), 0.25 (95% CI: 0.12-0.55), 22 (95% CI: 11-44), and 0.90 (95% CI: 0.87-0.92) respectively.

Conclusion

AI-based MRI can improve the accuracy of preoperative staging of patients with endometrial cancer to a certain extent. However, considering the limitations of this article, additional large-scale, prospective, multicenter clinical trials are necessary to further investigate the utility of AI-based MRI in the preoperative staging of endometrial cancer.

records.title: Efficacy of stability exercise-based treatment strategies for non-specific neck pain: a network meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of stability exercise-based treatment strategies for non-specific neck pain: a network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Non-specific neck pain (NSNP) is a common musculoskeletal disorder. Stability exercise is widely used in conservative management, but the relative efficacy of different exercise strategies remains unclear. This network meta-analysis evaluated stability exercise-based strategies for NSNP.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to November 24, 2025. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving adults with NSNP were included. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2.0. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was conducted, and continuous outcomes were expressed as mean differences (MDs) with 95% credible intervals (95% CrIs). Global consistency and convergence were assessed using ΔDIC and PSRF, respectively. The certainty of evidence for key comparisons was evaluated using CINeMA.

Results

Eighteen RCTs involving 950 participants were included; 10 studies were judged as low risk of bias, 4 as having some concerns, and 4 as high risk. Global consistency and convergence were acceptable (all ΔDIC < 5; PSRF = 1), with low-to-moderate heterogeneity across outcomes. For pain, several stability exercise strategies significantly reduced visual analog scale (VAS) scores compared with self-organized exercise (SOE), with shoulder resistance training combined with chest flexibility training (SRT+CFT) showing the greatest estimated reduction (MD = -8.16, 95% CrI: -13.04 to -3.27). For function, no intervention showed a significant advantage for the neck disability index (NDI), although neck resistance training combined with core resistance training (NRT+CRT) had the highest SUCRA value (MD = -27.43, 95% CrI: -58.28 to 3.90). For range of motion (ROM), neck flexibility training combined with NRT (NFT+NRT) had the highest SUCRA values for neck flexion, extension, bilateral lateral flexion, and bilateral rotation. The certainty of evidence was generally low or very low, with few moderate-certainty estimates.

Conclusion

Stability exercise-based strategies showed outcome-specific effects in NSNP. NRT, SRT, CRT, NFT, and their combinations may be more beneficial for pain relief and ROM improvement, whereas no clear superiority was found for functional recovery. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because certainty was generally low or very low and several treatment nodes were supported by limited evidence.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/, identifier CRD420251243575.

records.title: ChatGPT and Other Large Language Models in Inflammatory Arthritis: A Systematic Review Across Clinical Tasks.

content.title: ChatGPT and Other Large Language Models in Inflammatory Arthritis: A Systematic Review Across Clinical Tasks.
content.abstract:
Objective

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated for rheumatology tasks, but their performance in inflammatory arthritis (IA) remains unclear. We systematically reviewed LLM performance across clinical tasks in IA.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420261359100), searching PubMed, Scopus, and PubMed Central from January 2022 to April 2026 for studies evaluating LLM performance on clinical tasks in IA. Two reviewers (YA, AG) screened 113 records.

Results

Eighteen studies covered rheumatoid arthritis (n = 3), axial spondyloarthritis (n = 7), psoriatic arthritis (n = 2), gout (n = 1), juvenile idiopathic arthritis (n = 1), and multiple diseases (n = 4). Most diseases and tasks were represented by only 1 to a few studies, and the evidence base remains early stage and uneven across conditions. Over 20 distinct LLMs were evaluated, including ChatGPT-3.5 to ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Claude, and Perplexity; ChatGPT/GPT variants were the most frequently tested models (16/18 studies), so the current evidence base is predominantly ChatGPT/GPT-based. Findings spanned patient education (n = 11), guideline adherence (n = 6), clinical reasoning (n = 3), and other applications (n = 1). All readability assessments exceeded the recommended thresholds. Guideline concordance ranged from 48% to 96%. Accuracy was lower for case-based clinical scenarios (4.24/6) than for frequently asked questions and guideline-based questions (5.32-5.36/6; P = 0.04). When compared with real clinical data, agreement was poor (Cohen and Fleiss κ ≈ 0).

Conclusion

LLMs may support patient education, factual medication queries, and structured guideline questions when used under clinician review, but should not be used for case-based reasoning, treatment selection, or autonomous clinical decisions. None of the 18 included studies evaluated retrieval-augmented or agent-based systems, and none prospectively validated LLMs in clinical workflows. Safe integration in rheumatology will require purpose-built, knowledge-grounded systems and prospective evaluation before routine clinical use.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in diagnosis of pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders: a scoping review.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in diagnosis of pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders: a scoping review.
content.abstract:
Background

Neurodevelopmental disorders are a group of conditions that affect key areas of development and may significantly impact a child's quality of life. This underscores the importance of accurate diagnostic tools to improve outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown measurable effectiveness for enhancing the diagnosis and monitoring of neurodevelopmental disorders. This scoping review aims to summarize the current evidence on the use of AI technologies, including deep learning, supervised machine learning, decision support systems, and biosignal analysis, in improving diagnostic accuracy for pediatric neurodevelopmental disorders.

Data sources

A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, LILACS, MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and psychology-indexed journals, covering publications from 2000 to January 2025. Keywords and Medical Subject Headings terms were used to search for and select studies, applying specific inclusion and exclusion criteria. Selection followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines and included clinical studies, reviews, and validation research. The data were extracted and synthesized descriptively.

Results

Twenty-two studies were included. Deep learning models achieved diagnostic accuracies exceeding 85% in most studies in neuroimaging interpretation, whereas supervised machine learning improved the subtype classification of autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Decision support systems have increased diagnostic efficiency, and biosignal-based AI has shown potential in identifying physiological markers related to neurodevelopmental disorders.

Conclusions

AI technologies may significantly contribute to improving early diagnosis and clinical decision-making in pediatric neurodevelopment. However, variability in study design, population, and algorithm standardization remains a challenge. AI technologies are also facing ethical concerns such as data privacy and security, interpretability, equity and access, and algorithmic bias. Further multicenter validation and regulatory frameworks are essential for clinical translation.

records.title: A meta-analysis of the incidence proportion of obesity and associated risk factors in patients with schizophrenia.

content.title: A meta-analysis of the incidence proportion of obesity and associated risk factors in patients with schizophrenia.
content.abstract:
Objective

This meta-analysis aimed to investigate the incidence proportion of obesity and its influencing factors in patients with schizophrenia (SCH).

Methods

A comprehensive literature search was conducted using a combination of MeSH subject headings and free-text terms across multiple databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, and SinoMed. The search covered all publications up to May 26, 2025. Meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4 and Stata 18.0 software.

Results

A total of 18 studies involving 9, 351 patients with SCH were included in the analysis. This meta-analysis revealed that the incidence proportion of obesity in patients with SCH was 33.0%. Additionally, the following factors were significantly associated with an elevated risk of obesity in this population (P < 0.05): female sex (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.10-1.20), elevated FG (OR = 1.08, 95% CI = 1.04-1.12), diabetes (OR = 2.36, 95% CI = 1.79-3.10), elevated TG (OR = 1.13, 95% CI = 1.08-1.18), high LDL (OR = 1.88, 95% CI = 1.45-2.44), olanzapine use (OR = 7.40, 95% CI = 4.98-11.00), combined antipsychotic therapy (OR = 3.19, 95% CI = 2.31-4.41), use of typical antipsychotics (OR = 1.46, 95% CI = 1.18-1.82), use of atypical antipsychotics (OR = 1.70, 95% CI = 1.42-2.03), high red blood cell count (OR = 2.80, 95% CI = 1.60-4.90), and low HDL (OR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.41-2.16).

Conclusion

Current evidence indicates that the major risk factors for obesity in patients with SCH include female sex, elevated FG, diabetes, high TG levels, elevated LDL, use of olanzapine, combined antipsychotic treatment, use of typical antipsychotics, use of atypical antipsychotics, higher red blood cell count, and reduced HDL levels. Clinicians should implement early screening and targeted interventions to mitigate the development of obesity in this population, thereby improving their overall quality of life.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251121298.

records.title: Systematic review of atropine cost-effectiveness in childhood myopia management.

content.title: Systematic review of atropine cost-effectiveness in childhood myopia management.
content.abstract:
Background

Childhood myopia is a global public health concern, with rising prevalence and a significant economic burden due to complications like retinal detachment and macular degeneration. Low-dose atropine (LDA) range 0.01%-0.05% is a clinically effective intervention for slowing myopia progression. However, its economic value remains under-evaluated across diverse settings.

Methods and findings

We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251009680) to assess the cost-effectiveness of atropine for myopia management in children. Four model-based economic evaluations met the inclusion criteria, from Hong Kong, New Zealand, Australia/China and France/United Kingdom. Two studies used Markov cohort state-transition models while two employed a cohort decision-analytic model with probabilistic simulation of refractive outcomes. All four economic evaluations adopted a societal perspective; each applied a 3% annual discount rate to costs in their analyses and reported sensitivity analyses around discounting. Time horizons ranged from 5 years for incident myopia to lifetime horizons capturing myopia complications and vision impairment. Across economic models, LDA was consistently found to be cost-effective or cost-saving compared with standard care. Reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) included approximately NZ$1,590 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained in a New Zealand Markov cost-utility model, and USD 220-275 per diopter spherical equivalent reduction in a 5-year Hong Kong cost-effectiveness analysis. Evidence from high- and middle-income settings indicates that low-dose atropine is a cost-effective strategy, particularly when long-term progression to high myopia and its associated complications is considered. In European settings, low-dose atropine demonstrated a favorable cost profile compared with standard correction in children at higher risk of myopia progression, with consistent findings of cost-neutrality or cost savings when downstream costs of high myopia were included.

Conclusion

Studies demonstrate favourable economic value using diverse metrics, including cost per diopter reduction, cost ratios, and cost-utility estimates, rather than uniformly reported ICERs. Greater economic benefits are observed over longer time horizons, largely driven by the avoidance of high myopia-related complications and associated costs.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251009680, identifier PROSPERO CRD420251009680.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based screening of phytochemicals for targeted cancer therapy.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based screening of phytochemicals for targeted cancer therapy.
content.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide and continues to pose a serious public health challenge. The limited success of many current treatments-often due to toxicity, poor selectivity, and the development of drug resistance-highlights the need for new and more effective therapeutic options. Phytochemicals have emerged as a valuable source of anticancer agents, offering rich structural diversity and a wide range of biological activities. However, identifying promising compounds from the vast chemical space of natural products remains difficult using conventional screening methods, which are typically slow, costly, and inefficient. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has begun to transform phytochemical-based drug discovery. Machine learning and deep learning approaches are now used to support key steps in the discovery process, including metabolite identification, virtual screening, target prediction, and toxicity assessment. By integrating chemical, biological, and multi-omics data, AI enables a more systematic and data-driven exploration of natural product diversity. Despite these advances, challenges persist, particularly the scarcity of high-quality experimental data, the structural complexity of phytochemicals, and their limited representation in public databases. This review critically examines current AI applications in phytochemical-based anticancer drug discovery and discusses emerging strategies aimed at overcoming these limitations. Overall, AI-driven phytochemical screening represents a promising path toward accelerating the development of next-generation cancer therapies.

records.title: Diagnostic Potential of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting Vertical Root Fractures on Dental Imaging: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Potential of Artificial Intelligence for Detecting Vertical Root Fractures on Dental Imaging: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Unlabelled

Vertical root fracture (VRF) remains a diagnostic challenge because radiographic signs are often subtle, non-specific and influenced by imaging modality, fracture characteristics, artefacts and observer interpretation. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for VRF detection on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), periapical radiographs and panoramic radiographs and evaluated the certainty of evidence. This review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies recommendations and was prospectively registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews. Studies evaluating AI-based models for VRF detection on dental imaging were included. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using bivariate random-effects models when complete 2 × 2 contingency tables were available. Summary receiver operating characteristic curves were generated. Risk of bias was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach adapted for diagnostic test accuracy. Post-hoc sensitivity analyses retained one representative dataset per study to assess the influence of multiple model-specific datasets. Six studies were included, of which 4 contributed to quantitative synthesis. The CBCT-based AI models showed high diagnostic performance under predominantly controlled or partially controlled conditions, with a pooled sensitivity of 85.3% and specificity of 89.0% (area under the curve [AUC]=0.921). The CBCT convolutional neural network-only subgroup showed sensitivity of 88.3% and specificity of 87.6% (AUC=0.929). Periapical radiograph-based models showed high sensitivity but limited specificity, with pooled sensitivity of 86.9% and specificity of 61.2% (AUC=0.708). The probabilistic neural network-only periapical subgroup improved sensitivity, but specificity remained limited. Sensitivity analyses confirmed preserved CBCT performance and persistently low periapical specificity. Panoramic radiography was assessed qualitatively because complete 2 × 2 data were unavailable. Certainty of evidence was moderate for CBCT and low for periapical radiographs. AI-based models show promising diagnostic potential for VRF detection, particularly on CBCT. However, current evidence mainly reflects performance under controlled or partially controlled conditions and should not be interpreted as definitive real-world diagnostic effectiveness. AI should currently be considered an adjunctive decision-support tool rather than an autonomous diagnostic method, especially for 2-dimensional imaging modalities. Prospective, multicentre clinical validation studies are needed.

records.title: The impact of statin therapy on the prognosis of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The impact of statin therapy on the prognosis of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Statins are increasingly recognized for their potential to reduce endocrine therapy resistance and improve overall survival in breast cancer. However, their specific prognostic impact on hormone receptor-positive (HR+) breast cancer remains incompletely understood. This study aims to evaluate the effect of statin use on recurrence and mortality in HR+ breast cancer patients through a comprehensive meta-analysis.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science for studies comparing the outcomes of statin users versus non-users among HR+ breast cancer patients. Hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using appropriate statistical models.

Results

The meta-analysis incorporated 7 studies encompassing 267,913 HR+ breast cancer patients. Pooled analyses demonstrated that statin use was significantly associated with a 23% reduction in recurrence risk (HR = 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.98, P = 0.03) and a significant decrease in mortality (HR = 0.77; 95% CI: 0.73-0.81, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings.

Conclusion

Our large-scale meta-analysis suggests that statin therapy confers a protective effect against recurrence and mortality in HR+ breast cancer. These findings highlight the promising role of statins as an effective adjunctive therapy and underscore the necessity for future large-scale, prospective trials to optimize their clinical applications.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024599286, identifier CRD42024599286.

records.title: Risk prediction models for malnutrition in patients with cancer: a systematic review.

content.title: Risk prediction models for malnutrition in patients with cancer: a systematic review.
content.abstract:
Background

At present, many nutritional risk prediction models have been developed for cancer patients, but there is still uncertainty regarding the methodological quality and clinical applicability of these models.

Objective

To systematically review and critically appraise existing risk prediction models for malnutrition in cancer patients.

Methods

The PubMed, EBSCO, Medline, Web of Science, Scopus and Cochrane Library databases were systematically retrieved. The retrieval period was from the establishment of the databases to September 30, 2025. Based on the Predictive Model Bias Risk of Assessment Tool (PROBAST) and Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies (CHARMS), two independent authors conducted a rigorous assessment and data extraction of the study.

Results

A total of 6,343 articles were retrieved, ultimately including 16 studies and 42 models. The sample size included in the studies ranged from 120 to 4,487. Models were developed with logistic regression or machine-learning algorithms. The area under the curve (AUC) for the development cohort ranged from 0.745 to 1.000, while for the validation cohort ranged from 0.687 to 0.982. Twelve studies (75.0%) evaluated model calibration using calibration curves, the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and the Brier score, demonstrating good calibration performance. All risk prediction models have a relatively high risk of bias, primarily due to issues with the study population and analysis domain, two models (12.5%) raised high concern regarding applicability.

Conclusion

Research on prediction models for malnutrition in cancer patients is still in the development stage. The predictive performance of the developed models is generally acceptable, but there are still deficiencies in validation and evaluation.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery: a deep learning paradigm shift in pharmaceutical research and development.
content.abstract: Efficient drug discovery is essential to mitigate the high attrition rates and capital-intensive nature of traditional pharmaceutical research. Deep learning (DL) has catalyzed a paradigm shift, offering unprecedented computational capabilities to accelerate this process. This review systematically summarizes advancements in DL methodologies for drug discovery. First, the critical data foundations, Molecular Representation Learning, and core architectures underpinning artificial intelligence (AI)-driven therapeutics are elucidated, with a particular emphasis on the evolution of generative AI frameworks (such as Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and diffusion models) for chemical space exploration. Subsequently, diverse DL applications across the discovery pipeline are investigated, encompassing target identification, virtual screening, de novo molecular design, retrosynthetic analysis, absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) profiling, and drug repurposing. Furthermore, persistent challenges, particularly data scarcity, model opacity, experimental validation bottlenecks, and escalating computational resource requirements, are critically evaluated. To bridge the gap between in silico predictions, chemical synthesis, and biological reality, emerging solutions such as federated learning, causality-aware Explainable AI (XAI), closed-loop autonomous laboratories, and efficiency-oriented algorithmic strategies are explored. Ultimately, this article provides strategic insights into leveraging DL, underscoring its transformative potential in driving next-generation medicinal and therapeutic innovation.

records.title: Acromegaly and breast cancer risk: evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Acromegaly and breast cancer risk: evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Acromegaly is a rare endocrine disorder characterized by chronic excess growth hormone (GH) and elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), which are known to have mitogenic and anti-apoptotic effects on breast tissue. While an increased risk of several malignancies has been observed in patients with acromegaly, the relationship between acromegaly and breast cancer remains unclear.

Objective

To systematically evaluate the incidence and prevalence of breast cancer in patients with acromegaly and assess whether a consistent oncologic risk exists in this population.

Methods

We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception through early 2025 for studies reporting breast cancer in acromegaly. Citation tracking identified additional reports. After screening, 24 studies (>17,000 patients) were included, with data on cancer frequency, timing, and GH/IGF-1 levels extracted for analysis. From a subset of these studies reporting standardized incidence ratios (SIR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), a random-effects meta-analysis was performed to generate a pooled SIR, accounting for between-study heterogeneity.

Results

This systematic review of 24 studies with diverse designs, encompassing 17,413 patients with acromegaly, found breast cancer prevalence ranging from 0.42% to 5.85%. Several studies reported elevated GH and IGF-1 levels at any cancer diagnosis, but methodological heterogeneity limited conclusions on dose-response or temporal associations. Ten studies reported SIRs with 95% CIs and were included in the pooled analysis. The pooled SIR for breast cancer among patients with acromegaly was 1.20 (95% CI: 0.94-1.54), with moderate heterogeneity (I² = 58%).

Conclusion

Although there is a strong biological rationale for a link between GH/IGF-1 excess and breast cancer, current clinical studies have not shown a clear or consistently increased risk in patients with acromegaly. The mixed results likely reflect issues such as surveillance bias, differences in study designs, and limited adjustment for confounders. For now, breast cancer screening in this population should generally follow the same guidelines as the general population, with perhaps closer attention in patients who have poorly controlled disease. Moving forward, well-designed prospective studies that track cancer outcomes in relation to biochemical disease activity and control will be key to answering this question.

records.title: Ontology-based approaches for multi-destination tourism planning: a systematic literature review.

content.title: Ontology-based approaches for multi-destination tourism planning: a systematic literature review.
content.abstract: Tourism planning is becoming increasingly complex as travel behavior shifts from single-destination visits to multi-destination itineraries. However, many tourism information systems still rely on point-of-interest data and recommendation algorithms that lack the semantic structures needed to represent relationships between destinations. This limitation is important in smart tourism environments that require interoperable, data-integrated systems to support meaningful travel planning. This study conducts a systematic literature review of ontology and knowledge graph-based approaches for tourism planning to assess their ability to support itinerary modelling. Using PRISMA guidelines, relevant studies were retrieved from Scopus, ScienceDirect and IEEE Xplore, with 21 articles meeting all eligibility criteria. The review identifies six themes: ontology and semantic modelling, knowledge graph construction and enrichment, tourism recommendation and personalization, semantic retrieval and question answering, route planning and decision support, and itinerary-level and multi-destination representation. The analysis shows that ontology and knowledge graphs are widely used to organize tourism knowledge and enhance recommendation systems. However, most studies remain focused on entity-level modelling, while explicit semantic modelling of itinerary-level constructs remains limited. This gap highlights the need for ontology frameworks that can formally represent travel sequences and inter-destination dependencies to better support smart-tourism planning.

records.title: The efficacy of extracorporeal photopheresis in the treatment of steroid refractory acute graft-versus-host disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The efficacy of extracorporeal photopheresis in the treatment of steroid refractory acute graft-versus-host disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease (SR-aGVHD) is a significant complication of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) represents a key second-line option. Previous reviews have provided valuable insights, and recent studies allow for an updated synthesis of efficacy, safety, and patterns of ECP use in SR-aGVHD, including outcomes not fully analysed previously. This study aims to address the literature gap by providing a comprehensive updated review of the efficacy of ECP and its patterns of use in SR-aGVHD.

Materials and methods

A Systematic literature search was conducted as per PRISMA guidelines, up to September 2024, using the PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane databases. Studies investigating the use of ECP in the setting of chronic GVHD, GVHD prophylaxis, or first-line treatment of aGVHD were excluded. Meta-analyses using fixed and random effects models were employed to estimate the pooled effect sizes.

Results

Thirty-eight studies, including a total of 1249 participants, were included, and 29 were included in the quantitative analyses. Most studies focused on the adult population, and the majority used a retrospective single-arm study design (n = 30). Overall, skin, gut, and liver response rates were 72%, 89%, 54%, and 36%, respectively. The pooled steroid-sparing percentage was 66%. ECP showed significantly higher survival in patients with grade 2 GVHD compared with grades 3 and 4 (HR: 2.35, 95% CI: 1.67 - 3.29). ECP demonstrated a positive trend in overall survival compared to other treatments, but the results were not significant.

Conclusion

This review indicates that ECP is an effective treatment for SR-aGVHD, with favorable response and survival outcomes. However, due to the heterogeneity observed in the analyses among the studies, more controlled trials are needed to establish its effects in combination with other agents and against other regimens.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD42024585471.

records.title: Role of artificial intelligence in gastric diseases.

content.title: Role of artificial intelligence in gastric diseases.
content.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in gastroenterology has evolved from basic computer-aided detection to sophisticated multimodal frameworks that enable real-time clinical decision support. This study presents AI applications in gastric disease diagnosis and management, highlighting the transition from domain-specific deep learning to general-purpose large language models. Our research reveals a key finding: AI effectiveness demonstrates an inverse relationship with user expertise, with moderate-expertise practitioners benefiting the most, whereas experts and novices show limited performance gains. We developed a clinical decision support system achieving 96% lesion detection internally and 82%-87% classification accuracy in external validation. Multimodal integration, which combines endoscopic images, clinical histories, laboratory results, and genomic data, enables comprehensive disease assessment and personalized treatment. The emergence of large language models with expanding context windows and multiagent architectures represents a paradigm shift in medical AI. Furthermore, emerging technologies are expanding AI's potential applications, and feasibility studies on smart glasses in endoscopy training suggest opportunities for hands-free assistance, although clinical implementation challenges persist. This minireview addresses persistent limitations including geographic bias in training data, regulatory hurdles, ethical considerations regarding patient privacy and AI accountability, and the concentration of AI development among technology giants. Successful integration requires balancing innovation with patient safety, while preserving the irreplaceable role of human clinical judgment.

records.title: A Hybrid Large Language Model and Diffusion Framework for Rational Promoter Design.

content.title: A Hybrid Large Language Model and Diffusion Framework for Rational Promoter Design.
content.abstract: High-performance promoters are essential tools for precisely regulating gene expression, yet their rational design within the vast combinatorial sequence space remains a major challenge. Here, we present a hybrid framework that integrates a large language model (LLM) with a diffusion model to enable data-driven and interpretable promoter design. The fine-tuned LLM predicts promoter strength with high accuracy and, through systematic sequence mutations, identifies biologically essential core regions. A diffusion model is then conditioned on these core regions to reconstruct non-core regions and generate complete promoter sequences. We experimentally validated this approach in Escherichia coli by high-throughput barcoded promoter activity sequencing: 7.78% of the designed promoters outperformed the benchmark promoter BBa_J23119, with the best variants reaching approximately 2.5-fold the expression level of BBa_J23119. By explicitly coupling interpretability with generative design, this strategy provides a practical framework for promoter design in E. coli and may be adaptable to other regulatory sequence engineering tasks.

records.title: Ethical Risks of Medical AI Agents and a Governance Framework: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Policy Responses.

content.title: Ethical Risks of Medical AI Agents and a Governance Framework: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Policy Responses.
content.abstract: This systematic review identified ethical risks associated with medical AI agents and developed a governance framework adapted to China's healthcare context. PubMed, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched for records published or publicly released between January 1, 2020 and 30 June 2025. Of 1239 records identified, 837 underwent title and abstract screening, 68 were assessed in full, and 58 were included in the synthesis. The evidence base comprised 12 core agentic sources, 24 agent-focused boundary sources, and 22 governance, policy, legal, or normative sources. Eight non-exclusive ethical-risk themes were identified, led by safety, reliability, and hallucination; accountability and liability; bias and fairness; and privacy and security. Core agentic evidence indicated that multi-step execution, external tool use, persistent memory, and multi-agent coordination may amplify error propagation, provenance, privacy, and responsibility-allocation risks. Six representative cases and governance events were analyzed separately using the Four Principles of Biomedical Ethics to examine how similar risks arise across different technologies, jurisdictions, and institutional settings. The synthesis informed a four-component governance framework linking ethical and legal challenges, biomedical ethical principles, operational governance mechanisms, and expected outcomes. The proposed mechanisms include lifecycle risk monitoring, human oversight and escalation, responsibility allocation, privacy and data governance, documentation and auditability, fairness and equitable-access safeguards, and multistakeholder ethics review. The framework is intended as a policy-oriented and institutionally adaptable proposal rather than a validated intervention and requires prospective evaluation in specific cases of healthcare organizations and governance events.

records.title: The Formal-Functional Gap: How Artificial Intelligence Reshapes Medical Professional Identity.
records.publisher: Advances in medical education and practice

content.title: The Formal-Functional Gap: How Artificial Intelligence Reshapes Medical Professional Identity.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into clinical practice and medical education, yet research on AI and medical professional identity has largely evolved in parallel.

Objective

To examine how AI is transforming fundamental components of medical professional identity and propose a framework for understanding its implications for professional identity formation in medical education.

Methods

This narrative review synthesizes conceptual, empirical, and theoretical literature on AI, professional identity formation, and clinical practice through iterative literature searching and citation tracking. Peer-reviewed studies, regulatory data, and national survey reports were considered.

Results

AI affects professional identity unevenly. Diagnostic, predictive, generative, and emerging autonomous systems most directly influence expertise, clinical reasoning, and professional autonomy, shifting physicians from exclusive holders of specialized knowledge toward validators of increasingly accessible but variably trusted information. Evidence of automation bias and reduced diagnostic performance highlights this transition. We conceptualize the divergence between the formal locus of clinical responsibility, which remains with physicians, and the functional locus of influence decisions, shared with AI, as the formal-functional gap (FFG). Its magnitude varies by AI configuration, identity component, and career stage, potentially placing trainees at risk of never-skilling and experienced physicians at risk of deskilling. Ethical responsibility, humanistic care, lifelong learning, and professional authority are affected more indirectly.

Conclusion

AI-mediated professional identity change reflects a dynamic interaction between physicians' developmental trajectories and evolving AI capabilities. Medical education should prioritize sustained expertise, clinical reasoning, professional autonomy, AI-interpretive judgment, and human oversight. The FFG remains a conceptual framework whose relationships require empirical validation.

records.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.

content.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
content.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. Artificial intelligence and genome-scale systems biology have made it easy to generate metabolic hypotheses at a scale no experimental program could match - machine learning models trained on genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data now output candidate vulnerabilities, biomarkers, and drug combinations faster than they can be tested - but the resulting literature has not been consistently honest about how far any given prediction has actually traveled toward clinical relevance. We examine six areas where this gap is most visible: multi-omics data integration, genome-scale metabolic network modeling, computational discovery of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal interactions, single-cell and spatial resolution of metabolic heterogeneity, AI-guided drug and biomarker discovery, and the small set of studies that have actually reached clinical testing. Rather than summarizing these areas as separate literatures, we grade every substantive finding discussed against an explicit four-tier evidence standard - associative, mechanistic, perturbation-validated, or clinically tested - and we apply that standard critically rather than deferentially: several widely cited computational vulnerabilities remain unconfirmed outside the cell lines in which they were discovered, genome-scale models continue to carry unresolved gaps in reaction coverage that limit their predictive reach, and, of the AI-derived metabolic predictions discussed in this review, only one has so far been tested in a completed prospective clinical trial. We argue that this shortage of prospective validation, not a shortage of computational sophistication, is the field's central constraint, and we close by identifying where methodological effort would do the most good: standardized validation reporting, tissue-resolved rather than bulk metabolic models, and closer coupling between computational prediction and the specific experimental designs capable of falsifying it.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.

content.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
content.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Public Health: Integrated SPAR-4 Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Public Health: Integrated SPAR-4 Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming multiple sectors, including public health. Recent years have witnessed a substantial increase in research on integrating AI into public health systems, reflecting a growing interest in its potential to improve surveillance, diagnostics, policy development, and health outcomes.

Objective

This study aims to identify how AI has been applied in public health, examine its impact on the field, and determine future research directions at the intersection of AI and public health.

Methods

A systematic literature review was conducted to analyze existing scholarly research on AI applications in public health. Relevant studies were collected, screened, and categorized to identify dominant research themes and gaps in the literature.

Results

The analysis revealed five primary thematic clusters within the literature: (1) AI model development and performance, (2) public health threats and outbreak management, (3) systematic reviews and evidence synthesis, (4) social and ethical issues in public health, and (5) governance, policy, and innovation. The review also identified underexplored areas and inconsistencies across studies, highlighting significant research gaps.

Conclusions

AI has demonstrated substantial potential to enhance public health practice and research. However, further investigation is needed to address ethical, governance, and implementation challenges. Future research should focus on strengthening policy frameworks, improving transparency and accountability in AI systems, and promoting interdisciplinary collaboration to ensure the responsible and equitable integration of AI into public health.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.
content.abstract: This review examines the current status of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in the perioperative management of emergency trauma. Published studies suggest performance advantages of AI over traditional methods in prehospital triage, radiographic injury detection, massive transfusion prediction, and early warning of postoperative complications, although findings vary across study designs and validation settings. However, actual adoption in trauma care remains limited due to data heterogeneity, performance degradation in external validation, workflow integration challenges, lack of interpretability, and a scarcity of prospective interventional evidence. This review further argues that methodologically inflated benchmark performance constitutes an underrecognized barrier to adoption in its own right, and that bridging the implementation gap will likely require a shift from area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-centered reporting toward reporting sensitivity at prespecified clinical thresholds and evaluating patient outcomes in prospective interventional trials.

records.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
records.publisher: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

content.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-based tools are emerging across many areas of medicine. The next generation of medical professionals must be prepared to critically assess the tools they will use, including how they work and the ethical or legal implications of their implementation. To address this need, we developed a generalizable case-writing framework that enables educators and learners to engage with clinical cases integrating AI/ML concepts, clinical reasoning, and ethical considerations.

Methods

We designed a case-writing template to compose clinical case scenarios that integrate clinical, technical, and ethical/legal learning objectives relating to AI applications in medicine. Medical students used this template to construct 3 cases. Student-authored cases were presented to a broader audience in 1-hour sessions: first as a pilot event, then as a class-wide lecture for 140 fourth-year medical students in a transition-into-residency course.

Results

After the sessions, student audiences had a statistically significant increase in familiarity with key AI terminology, a greater appreciation for the importance of ethical considerations of AI applications in health care, and an increased perceived importance of integrating AI-related topics into the medical curriculum.

Discussion

A case-based framework provides a scalable approach to integrating AI education into existing curricula by connecting clinical scenarios with technical concepts and the ethical considerations of AI adoption; cases offer a familiar format that helps learners understand AI applications in patient care while exploring implementation challenges. The case-writing template and 3 sample cases are provided as adaptable resources for educators seeking to incorporate AI literacy.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
records.publisher: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

content.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation.

Results

Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation.

Conclusion

AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

records.title: Research progress of artificial intelligence applications in obstetrics.

content.title: Research progress of artificial intelligence applications in obstetrics.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across obstetrics, with applications spanning electronic medical record analysis, prenatal ultrasound, fetal monitoring, prediction of pregnancy complications, labor management, postpartum care, and telemedicine. The evidence reviewed in this article indicates that AI can improve automated information extraction, image and signal interpretation, and risk discrimination across multiple obstetric tasks, with particularly consistent advances in fetal ultrasound analysis, cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation, and early prediction of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. However, model performance is heterogeneous and is often reported using discrimination or classification metrics rather than patient-centered clinical outcomes. In CTG research, models differ substantially in whether they classify interpretation categories, detect fetal hypoxia or acidemia, or predict neonatal outcomes, making direct comparison difficult. Similarly, high predictive accuracy for pregnancy complications does not establish that AI implementation itself improves maternal or neonatal outcomes, and the clinical benefit of treatment should not be attributed to the predictive model without intervention studies. Across obstetric applications, limited external validation, dataset shift, class imbalance, calibration, interpretability, workflow integration, and data governance remain major barriers to clinical translation. This review therefore emphasizes the distinction between technical model performance and demonstrated clinical utility, and highlights the evidence required to move AI applications from retrospective development toward prospective, clinically integrated obstetric care.

records.title: Research progress and prospects of cochlear implant technology.

content.title: Research progress and prospects of cochlear implant technology.
content.abstract: Traditional cochlear implant systems depend on external devices and face challenges related to convenience, esthetics, and auditory performance in complex soundscapes. Recently, research has shifted from "functional substitution" to "functional enhancement" and "biological fusion." However, most emerging approaches remain in the preclinical, prototype verification, or early clinical stages, lacking substantial evidence of clinical benefits. This narrative review examines research progress across five key dimensions of cochlear implants: The electrode interface has advanced from passive implants to dynamic, adaptive, and biologically active intelligent interfaces. Signal processing strategies are moving toward intelligence and physiological adaptation, with deep learning primarily used for noise suppression and coding optimization; however, clinical application is limited by real-time performance and individual variability. Bionic sensing aims to replicate the energy conversion mechanism between hair cells and the basement membrane at the signal source, currently focusing on laboratory prototypes. Optogenetics-driven optical regulation offers high spatial selectivity but remains in the early preclinical stage. The development of fully implanted systems emphasizes internal energy supply, ultra-low power consumption processing, and system integration, marking a significant engineering direction for making devices "invisible." Each section of this article critically evaluates evidence maturity and transformation barriers, highlighting common challenges such as long-term biological stability, safety, energy consumption, and regulatory verification that must be addressed before large-scale clinical application. Future advancements will require collaboration among materials science, neuroscience, microelectronics, and artificial intelligence to create a two-way high-fidelity interface. The ultimate goal is not only to restore hearing but also to reconstruct a more natural auditory perception.

records.title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid cancer.

content.title: Application of artificial intelligence in the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid cancer.
content.abstract: Thyroid cancer is one of the most common endocrine malignancies, and its rising incidence has increased the demand for more accurate and efficient diagnostic and management strategies. Current clinical management mainly relies on ultrasonography, fine-needle aspiration (FNA), surgery, radioactive iodine therapy, thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression, and systemic treatment in selected advanced cases. However, substantial interobserver variability, indeterminate cytology, and heterogeneity in tumor behavior still complicate diagnosis and risk stratification. In thyroid cancer, AI(Artificial intelligence) -assisted models have been applied to ultrasound, CT, MRI, cytology, histopathology, and genomic data, with promising performance in distinguishing benign from malignant nodules, predicting lymph node metastasis and key mutations, and supporting individualized management. This review critically synthesizes evidence across these applications, focusing on study design, validation strategies, generalizability, and clinical relevance. It also examines explainable AI, emerging foundation models, and regulatory and implementation challenges. Although many models report high diagnostic or predictive performance, these results alone do not establish improvements in clinical decision-making or patient outcomes. Prospective clinical validation, cost-effectiveness assessment, and evaluation of integration into clinical workflows are needed to determine whether AI provides meaningful benefits over standard care.

records.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water

content.title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water
content.abstract: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Coronary Syndromes: Linking Cellular Pathways to Precision Risk Prediction.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Coronary Syndromes: Linking Cellular Pathways to Precision Risk Prediction.
content.abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) are no longer defined only by fixed stenosis of the epicardial coronary arteries. CCSs reflect a dynamic biological process. Key contributors include endothelial activation, lipid retention, macrophage foam-cell formation, vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching, and extracellular matrix remodelling. Microvascular rarefaction, perivascular adipose tissue inflammation, cardiometabolic comorbidity, and biological ageing add further complexity. This broader cellular and molecular model provides a rationale for artificial intelligence (AI), because conventional tools often assess anatomy, physiology, inflammation, and systemic biology in isolation. In this narrative review, we examine how AI and machine learning may support a more mechanistic and individualised approach to CCS by linking cellular pathways to measurable clinical signatures. We focus on AI-enabled plaque phenotyping, non-invasive physiology and ischaemia modelling, assessment of coronary microvascular dysfunction, perivascular inflammation mapping, and the integration of multi-omics with cardiometabolic risk profiling. Most of these tools, however, provide imaging-based or data-derived surrogates rather than direct measurements of endothelial activation, inflammation, or calcification biology. Within this limitation, current evidence suggests that AI can quantify subvisual high-risk plaque features, support non-invasive flow assessment, detect imaging patterns associated with microvascular dysfunction and perivascular inflammation, and, in research settings, relate molecular signatures to long-term cardiovascular risk. Clinical adoption remains constrained by retrospective study designs, limited external validation, heterogeneous imaging protocols, gaps in explainability, regulatory uncertainty, and algorithmic bias across sex, ethnicity, age, and resource settings. Future work should prioritise prospective trials, transparent reporting, federated validation, clinically interpretable outputs, and integration with guideline-based decision pathways. The greatest value of AI in CCS is likely to lie in augmenting mechanistic risk stratification and enabling precision prevention for patients whose risk is poorly captured by anatomy alone.

records.title: Ethical considerations in generative artificial intelligence for synthetic data generation in ophthalmology.
records.publisher: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie

content.title: Ethical considerations in generative artificial intelligence for synthetic data generation in ophthalmology.
content.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to reshape medical research, with ophthalmology at the forefront of this transformation. This narrative review examines the ethical considerations and challenges of using generative AI - particularly Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models - to create synthetic data for ophthalmic research. Synthetic data offers genuine solutions to long-standing obstacles: data scarcity, augmentation of datasets for rare diseases, and privacy-preserving multi-institutional collaboration. Yet the same capabilities introduce formidable risks.
